edges.limitations: Zebrafish haematopoiesis is not human marrow, the model does not carry a patient allele, and the myelodysplastic features required a second engineered tp53 mutation rather than arising on their own.

nodes.description: Global, trilineage bone marrow failure, the defining feature. Present in all reported patients in the phenotype-refinement series.

evidence.snippet: All patients present features consistent with IBMFS: bone marrow failure, growth retardation, failure to thrive, developmental delay, recurrent infections, and skin, teeth or hair abnormalities.

evidence.reference_title: DNAJC21 Mutations Link a Cancer-Prone Bone Marrow Failure Syndrome to Corruption in 60S Ribosome Subunit Maturation.
evidence.snippet: Collectively, these findings demonstrate that mutations in DNAJC21 cause a cancer-prone BMF syndrome due to corruption of early nuclear rRNA biogenesis and late cytoplasmic maturation of the 60S subunit.

evidence.reference_title: DNAJC21 Mutations Link a Cancer-Prone Bone Marrow Failure Syndrome to Corruption in 60S Ribosome Subunit Maturation.
evidence.snippet: Characterization of mutations revealed impairment in interactions with cofactors (PA2G4, HSPA8, and ZNF622) involved in 60S maturation.

meta.presence: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (frameshift, nonsense or splice-site)

nodes.description: Transplantation is the established treatment for marrow failure in the inherited bone marrow failure syndromes, and one DNAJC21 patient has been reported in a transplanted cohort: a child in a 32-patient series of acquired severe aplastic anaemia and non-Fanconi IBMFS given an HLA-matched related graft after low-dose cyclophosphamide, fludarabine and anti-thymocyte globulin. It is recorded for that one patient's inclusion and not for an outcome: the series reports 93% event-free and 95% overall survival at three years across all 32 children, which is a cohort figure and says nothing about the DNAJC21 patient individually. No DNAJC21-specific transplant outcome has been published.

evidence.reference_title: Human leucocyte antigen-matched related haematopoietic stem cell transplantation using low-dose cyclophosphamide, fludarabine and thymoglobulin in children with severe aplastic anaemia.
evidence.snippet: Nine patients had deleterious mutations (two ERCC6L2, two ANKRD26, two TINF2, one LZTFL1, one RTEL1 and one DNAJC21).

nodes.description: Early nuclear rRNA biogenesis and late cytoplasmic 60S maturation are both corrupted. The measurable consequences in patient-derived cells are cytoplasmic accumulation of the 60S nuclear export factor PA2G4, which should have been recycled, aberrant ribosome profiles, reduced amounts of rRNA, and increased sensitivity to the transcriptional inhibitor actinomycin D. This is the step that makes the disease a ribosomopathy and places it with SBDS, EFL1 and SRP54.

evidence.reference_title: DNAJC21 Mutations Link a Cancer-Prone Bone Marrow Failure Syndrome to Corruption in 60S Ribosome Subunit Maturation.
evidence.snippet: Lymphoblastoid cells obtained from an affected individual exhibit increased sensitivity to the transcriptional inhibitor actinomycin D and reduced amounts of rRNA.

nodes.description: The phenotype-refinement series provides a checklist for clinical evaluation at diagnosis and at regular follow-up, prompted by the aplastic anaemia, the possible increased leukaemia risk and the multisystem features. Surveillance rather than treatment is what the literature for this disease actually supports.

evidence.snippet: Considering the aplastic anemia, the possible increased risk for leukemia, and the multisystemic features, we provide a checklist for clinical evaluation at diagnosis and regular follow-up.

nodes.description: A predisposition to myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukaemia, shared with the other Shwachman-Diamond spectrum genes SBDS and SRP54. One child in the founding cohort developed acute myeloid leukaemia. This is the reason the disease is described as cancer-prone and the reason surveillance is recommended.

evidence.snippet: SBDS, DNAJC21, and SRP54 variants have been associated with myeloid neoplasia

nodes.description: Low neutrophil count, the arm of the cytopenia that the zebrafish model links to nucleotide imbalance and that nucleoside supplementation corrected in that model.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of Dnajc21 leads to cytopenia and altered nucleotide metabolism in zebrafish.
evidence.snippet: Dnajc21 loss accurately recapitulated the neutropenia, anemia, and reduced growth seen in SDS patients with DNAJC21 mutations.

nodes.description: A role for Dnajc21 in nucleotide metabolism, uncovered in the zebrafish model by combined transcriptomics and metabolomics. Its interest is practical as well as mechanistic: supplying nucleosides from outside restored neutrophil counts in the model, which is the only intervention reported anywhere to correct a DNAJC21 phenotype. Whether this operates in patients is untested.

evidence.snippet: All patients present features consistent with IBMFS: bone marrow failure, growth retardation, failure to thrive, developmental delay, recurrent infections, and skin, teeth or hair abnormalities.

nodes.description: Defective ribosome maturation produces ribosomal stress. In haematopoietic progenitors this means impaired differentiation, accumulation of DNA damage and reduced proliferation, which is what the zebrafish model measures directly. Whether the cell death here is TP53-dependent is not established for DNAJC21: in the model a tp53 mutation had to be introduced deliberately to produce myelodysplastic features, which tests tp53's role in transformation rather than in the baseline cytopenia.

nodes.description: Low platelets as part of the marrow failure. In the first reported adult it was the presenting and essentially the only haematological finding, persistent and non-progressive, which is what led her reporters to suggest that DNAJC21 should be considered in adults with unexplained thrombocytopenia.

evidence.reference_title: DNAJC21-related thrombocytopenia in a young adult female.
evidence.snippet: Here we report the first adult patient; a 20-year-old female with a novel frameshift variant in DNAJC21 presents with thrombocytopenia, dysmorphic findings, and ovarian agenesis.

nodes.description: Global marrow failure affecting all three lineages, which is the feature that defines the syndrome and the reason the founding cohort was assembled from children who did not fit any existing bone marrow failure syndrome. The severity is variable: the first reported adult had isolated non-progressive thrombocytopenia.

nodes.description: A homozygous canonical splice-donor change at the exon 7 boundary, reported in a girl investigated for cytopenia and dysmorphism whose diagnosis came from a reanalysis of existing exome data. RNA sequencing showed that the variant skips exon 7, deleting 88 nucleotides, so the mechanism is demonstrated at the transcript level rather than predicted from the position of the change.

evidence.reference_title: A Rare Inherited Bone Marrow Failure Syndrome Disclosed by Reanalysis of the Exome Data of a Patient Evaluated for Cytopenia and Dysmorphic Features.
evidence.snippet: Reanalysis of the ES data revealed a homozygous splice-site variant in the DNAJC21 (NM_001012339.3:c.983+1G>A), causing Shwachman-Diamond Syndrome (SDS).

evidence.reference_title: A Rare Inherited Bone Marrow Failure Syndrome Disclosed by Reanalysis of the Exome Data of a Patient Evaluated for Cytopenia and Dysmorphic Features.
evidence.snippet: It was shown by the RNA sequencing that exon 7 was skipped, causing an 88-nucleotide deletion.

nodes.description: The first in vivo model of Dnajc21 deficiency. It reproduces cytopenia, reduced growth and defective protein synthesis, and it was used to show that the cytopenia comes from impaired haematopoietic differentiation, DNA damage and reduced proliferation. Adding a biallelic tp53 mutation produces myelodysplastic-neoplasia-like features, and nucleoside supplementation restores neutrophil counts.
